title: Returned Property Tax Refunds Paid Back into a Summit Tax and Insurance Reserve
content:
A taxing authority sometimes mails a property tax refund to the borrower for an installment that a Summit Tax and Insurance Reserve under Set-Aside Accounts paid and that a corrected bill later lowered. The part of that refund the borrower pays back into the reserve is the **kept amount of a returned property tax refund**.

## Rule

- For a property tax refund that a taxing authority mailed to the borrower and that the borrower pays back into a Summit Tax and Insurance Reserve, and only for such a refund, the reserve is credited with the kept amount of a returned property tax refund rather than the whole refunded amount. A returned hazard or flood insurance premium is settled by the rule written for it, and every other refund is credited under the general refund rule of Set-Aside Accounts.
- The credit references the reserve's payment of the overpaid installment, and where more than one paid installment of the tax year is overpaid, the reserve's payment of the paid property tax bill with the latest due date; it is dated the handling date.
- The kept amount of a returned property tax refund is not worked out until the annual property tax on file has been reviewed against every property tax bill received since it was last set.

Put another way, the kept amount is never worked out on an annual property tax that has not yet been reviewed against every property tax bill received since that figure was last set.

Where two or more paid installments of the tax year are overpaid, the credit points at the reserve's payment of whichever of those paid property tax bills has the latest due date.

## Tool: `return_tax_refund_0b9f20b8`

**What it does.** It pays money from a property tax refund that the taxing authority mailed to the borrower back into a Summit Tax and Insurance Reserve. The payment is credited to the reserve the same day as a refund credit that points at the reserve's original payment of the overpaid tax installment, and the reserve balance rises by that amount. Nothing is charged to or credited on the loan balance. The credit shows on the reserve at once.

**How it is invoked.** `return_tax_refund_0b9f20b8` is a customer-side tool: the agent unlocks it and hands it over, and the customer themselves runs it to make the payment.

**Parameters.**

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `setaside_id` | Reference number of the Summit Tax and Insurance Reserve that receives the money, as the set-aside account lookup returns it and the agent reads it out to the borrower | Identifier |
| `source_txn_ref` | Reference number of the reserve's original tax payment transaction that the refund relates to, as the set-aside transaction lookup returns it and the agent reads it out to the borrower | Identifier |
| `credit_amount` | The amount the borrower pays into the reserve | USD, 2 decimal places, positive, rounded to the cent |

**Return.** A receipt with `status` — the literal "credited" when the money was received and credited; `setaside_txn_id` — reference number of the new refund credit; `setaside_id` — the reserve credited; `source_txn_ref` — the original tax payment the credit relates to; `credit_amount` — the amount credited, 2 decimal places; `effective_date` — the date of the credit, YYYY-MM-DD; `setaside_balance` — the reserve balance after the credit, 2 decimal places.

**Hypothetical receipt.** A call with a credit of 125.00 against a reserve holding 2,000.00 returns status "credited", the new credit's reference, credit 125.00, the day's date and a balance of 2,125.00.
